S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient_info.stressor: When Jose and his wife moved into an older Fort Worth house that needed extensive remodeling, the work initially felt like a natural extension of his carpentry skills and family duty. As the renovation dragged on, ordinary concerns about wiring, dust, tools, and safety began to attach themselves to intrusive unwanted thoughts, and he responded with increasingly repetitive checking and corrective routines that went far beyond practical construction standards. Over time, the routines consumed so much of his day that he stopped pursuing paid trade work, avoided community projects he had once led, and his wife became worried that the house had become the center of an unmanageable cycle rather than a home. He entered psychiatric care after a primary-care visit for exhaustion and functional decline led to a referral to a bilingual outpatient mental health clinic.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: Even when I know I did the job right, these ugly thoughts keep jumping in that a loose wire I missed is going to burn the house down or a nail I left somewhere is going to hurt my wife, and I try to push them out but they come right back stronger.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: I’m here because I spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust in the house, checking and fixing them again and again until I’m worn out and still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I stopped taking paid carpentry jobs and pulled back from the community projects I used to help with because the house takes over my whole day. My wife handles more of the errands and decisions now because I get stuck there and end up exhausted.
